frame.x: feet east of the west fence, along the north fence
frame.y: feet south of the north fence, along the west fence
frame.alignment: The fences run within 0.2 degrees of true north-south and east-west, so +x is east and +y is south.

parcel_likely.note: Likely 10-acre legal parcel (330 x 1,320 ft) measured to the road centerlines; not surveyed.

grid.how: Column letter A-G west to east, row number 1-26 north to south, 50 ft cells. Example: B19 is x 50-100, y 900-950.

georef.datum: NAD83 (same as WGS84 / GPS to within about 1 m here)
georef.formula: lat = lat[0] + lat[1]*x + lat[2]*y; lon = lon[0] + lon[1]*x + lon[2]*y (x, y in feet; exact to under 1 cm across the lot)

utm.formula: E = E0 + 0.3048*(x*cos t - y*sin t); N = N0 - 0.3048*(x*sin t + y*cos t)

georef.check: The owner's Google Maps pin on the red shed falls 5 ft from the shed roof center measured on USGS imagery.
georef.source: Lot frame fitted to the four fence lines on USGS NAIP imagery (0.52 m pixels, UTM zone 11N).

orchard.how: Tree R(r)-C(c) stands at x = c1_x + (c - 1) * tree_spacing, plus even_row_offset in even rows, and y = r1_y - (r - 1) * row_spacing.

features.name: Middle line (owner's tape)
features.notes: Owner's tape, October 24, 2026, marked by a red tick on each fence. The A14 hydrant sits on this line, and the red shed's north building corner (not the north awning) is 79 ft south of it. The shed stays where the imagery and the GPS pin put it (north wall at y 746), so the line is 667 ft south of the north fence. Half the 1,291.9 ft fence is still 645.95 ft, 21 ft north of here. The drone-photo red lines (about 660 to 680 ft) match this tape better than 646. Good to about 5 ft, the shed's imagery accuracy. A tape from the northwest fence corner would confirm the 667.

features.name: Well head
features.notes: 18 ft east of the pump house's east wall, on the pump house's midline (moved 10 ft east of the first east-side mark). Drilled to 375 ft; the pump sits at 350 ft, 25 ft off the bottom. A 240 V, 3 hp pump pushes 18 to 22 gpm. The October 24, 2026 note had called the well 350 ft deep; that figure is the pump setting, not the drilled depth. The driller hit low flow at about 200 ft, then a high-pressure flow at about 300 ft, and kept going to 350 ft to set the pump below that zone. The owner recalls those readings from July 2021, five years before October 2026. Those strike depths are a recollection, not a driller's log. The lot sits on basalt lava, not Idaho batholith granite: the Idaho Geological Survey state map (M-9, 2012) maps this point as Pliocene and Miocene basalt. Owner, October 28, 2026.

This is the room inside the posts; its berm on the north side, retaining wall, cut slopes, and swales are on the greenhouse site plan. Planned for 2028 or 2029; a draft position, not staked.
